examples: I go to the traditional market on weekends.
I bought fruit at the market.
nuance: 시장 usually means an open traditional market with many small stalls, unlike a modern 마트.
mistakes: Saying 시장에서 가요 instead of 시장에 가요 for going there.

examples: I go to the supermarket in the evening.
I bought milk at the supermarket.
This supermarket is open until late.
nuance: 마트 refers to a large modern supermarket or discount store, often a big chain with many products.
mistakes: Using 마트 for a tiny corner shop, which is really a 가게 or 편의점.

usage: I go to the convenience store
I buy at the convenience store
examples: I often go to the convenience store at night.
I drank coffee at the convenience store.
Convenience stores are usually open 24 hours.
nuance: 편의점 is a small always-open store like CU or GS25, handy for snacks, drinks, and quick errands.
mistakes: Calling a large 마트 a 편의점; the size and selection are different.

examples: I went to the cafe with a friend.
I read a book at the cafe.
The coffee at this cafe is delicious.
nuance: 카페 means a coffee shop where people relax, chat, or study, not just a place to buy coffee fast.
mistakes: Mixing up 카페 with 커피; 카페 is the place and 커피 is the drink.

usage: I withdraw money at the bank
examples: I have to go to the bank tomorrow.
I exchanged money at the bank.
nuance: 은행 is a place for money matters such as savings, transfers, and currency exchange, important for newcomers.
mistakes: Writing 은행에서 가요 instead of 은행에 가요 when you mean going there.

usage: I take a walk in the park
examples: I go to the park every morning.
I ride a bicycle in the park.
nuance: 공원 is a public green space for walking, exercising, or resting, common in every Korean neighborhood.
mistakes: Saying 공원에서 가요 when you really mean 공원에 가요 for going there.

examples: I usually walk to the station.
I wait for my friend at the station.
This station has a lot of people.
nuance: 역 means a train or subway station and often combines with line or area names like 서울역.
mistakes: Confusing 역 (station) with 역할 (role); they look similar but differ.

usage: I go to the post office
I send it at the post office
examples: I go to the post office to send a parcel.
I sent a letter at the post office.
The post office is closed on weekends.
nuance: 우체국 handles mail, parcels, and some banking, useful when sending packages home or paying bills.
mistakes: Using 은행 for sending parcels; that service belongs to the 우체국.

usage: I go to the movie theater
I watch a movie at the theater
examples: I want to go to the movie theater this weekend.
I ate popcorn at the movie theater.
The seats at this theater are comfortable.
nuance: 영화관 is the building where you watch films, while 영화 is the movie itself, so keep them separate.
mistakes: Saying 영화에 가요 instead of 영화관에 가요 when you mean the building.

examples: I arrived at the hotel late in the evening.
I ate breakfast at the hotel.
This hotel is close to the station.
nuance: 호텔 is paid lodging for travelers, ranging from simple to luxury, and is used for short stays.
mistakes: Using 집 for a hotel stay; 호텔 is temporary paid lodging, not your home.

examples: I go to the shop in front of my house.
I bought bread at the shop.
nuance: 가게 is a general word for a small shop or store and can combine with goods like 꽃 가게 or 빵 가게.
mistakes: Using 가게 for a huge chain store, which is better called a 마트.

examples: I have been to that tall building.
I met my friend in the building.
nuance: 빌딩 usually means a large modern multi-story building, often for offices, borrowed from English.
mistakes: Using 빌딩 for a small house; a house is 집, not 빌딩.
